body: Rodeo Drive - Special Events - Holiday Program Committee
name: Rodeo Drive / Special Events / Holiday Program Committee Liaison Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  The Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Rodeo Drive/Special Events/Holiday
  Program Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Monday, August 12, 2024
  5:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  August 12, 2024 / 5:00 PM
  a. IN ATTENDANCE: Mayor Lester Friedman, Councilmember Mary Wells,
  Deputy City Manager Keith Sterling, Community Outreach Manager Magdalena
  Davis, Special Events Film Coordinator Patricia Betancourt, Rodeo Drive
  Committee President Kay Monica Rose, Symblaze Representative Josh
  Morgerman

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Proposal from the Rodeo Drive Committee for the 2024 Rodeo Drive Holiday
  Lighting Celebration on November 14, 2024, and Additional Holiday Programming:
  a. Presentation by Kay Monica Rose:
  i. The Holiday Lighting Celebration will be on Thursday, November 14th.
  ii. The Liaisons were presented with three options for the design of the street
  banners. Councilmember Wells thought all three options seemed flat, and
  staff promised to work on the lighting of the options.
  iii. Rodeo Drive and the adjacent blocks of Dayton and Brighton will be closed
  to traffic from 9:00 PM on November 13th through 6:00 AM on November
  15th.
  iv. The RDC moved the main stage to the intersection of Brighton Way and
  Rodeo Drive to provide a more unified guest experience.
  v. There will also be flat screen monitors along Rodeo Drive as well as two
  LED video walls along Wilshire and Santa Monica displaying the stage. The
  stage itself will also have a video wall.
  vi. Candy Cane “Street Sweepers” will provide pop up dance performances
  along the street.
  vii. The 15 ft inflatable Reindeer will be present with the reindeer attendants
  and holiday helpers.
 Highlights for August 12, 2024
Rodeo Drive/Special Events/Holiday Program Committee

  viii. The event will also feature a nutcracker on stilts, snowmen puppets, roller
  skating performers, and bike propelled platforms with hula hoops and
  ribbons.
  ix. The stage performers will be Greg Scott, Red Hot Holiday Band, Holiday
  Harmony Carolers, Holiday Host – Cory, and the Blue Grass Strings. They
  will be followed by a holiday trio with Crooner, the Candy Cane Street
  Sweepers, a Yuletide Irish Dance Ensemble, and holiday ballroom dancers
  with vocals.
  x. Additional options for stage performers could include a headline
  performance, a tilted performer, sway poles, or a Holiday Drone Swarm.
  xi. A headliner was not included this year in order to save on costs.
  xii. The street lighting will feature UCLA’s Scattertones A Capella group as well
  as performing arts students from BHHS.
  xiii. The finale will consist of Santa’s arrival and a fireworks ceremony.
  xiv. This year’s event will consist of two wine gardens on the 200 and 400
  blocks of Rodeo Drive.
  xv. The event will be done in partnership with the Chamber of Commerce and
  the Conference and Visitor’s Bureau, who will promote the celebration on
  their social media pages as well as by sending out over 10,000 newsletters
  and emails.
  xvi. This year’s event will cost $1,553,468 as opposed to 2023, which cost
  $1,486.507. Without including the cost of the décor the celebration will cost
  $1,028,966 as opposed to 2023 which cost $ 1,000,547.
  b.  The garage is used for both event parking as well as for fireworks.
  c.  The $28,000 increase for the event itself is mostly due to increased labor costs,
  which increased from $142,000 in 2023 to $172,000 this year.
  d.  The RDC wished to add a second wine garden due to how packed it was at last
  year’s event.
  e.  The reason for the lack of headliner is that staff has found that this event has
  become a destination in its own right, outside of any headliner, and so cutting the
  headliner would save on talent costs while not affecting attendance numbers.
  f.  The rain contingency equipment has been budgeted for this year, which was
  around $24,000.
  g.  The two stages used in previous years was due to a desire to separate people
  during COVID. They are not using an area closer to Wilshire in order to allow space
  for the second wine garden and to bring more life to the 400 block of Rodeo.
  h.  The Mayor is concerned about the stage not being visible from Rodeo due to being
  on Brighton.
  i.  Both Liaisons are concerned about the cost of the event.
  j.  This item will return at an upcoming Liaison meeting for additional discussion to
  resolve the Liaisons concerns.

  3) Review and Selection of Citywide Holiday Streetpole Banner Designs:
  a. Presentation by Josh Morgerman:
  i. City Banners have a lifespan of about three years due to both physical
  deterioration and to refresh the look of the banners.
  ii. Option A is banners featuring ribbons wrapping around either Beverly Hills
  icons or Holiday Symbols.
 Highlights for August 12, 2024
Rodeo Drive/Special Events/Holiday Program Committee

  iii. Option B is Celebrate Here, which has one set of banners with graphics of
  the holidays while the other set has Celebrate Here written on it.
  iv. Option C features celebratory graphics with the word Together featuring
  prominently.
  b.  Staff mostly had “Ribbons” as their preferred option.
  c.  Councilmember Wells likes all three options, but has C as her first choice and A
  as her second choice.
  d.  Mayor Friedman is not a fan of negative space on banners, and likes option C, but
  is concerned about the alcohol on display.
  e.  Staff will move forward with option C, and will refine options and will address the
  concerns about the alcohol.

  4) Request from Young Israel of North Beverly Hills to Host Simchat Torah Celebration
  on October 24, 2024:
  a. Presentation by Patricia Betancourt:
  i. Young Israel of North Beverly Hills is requesting approval for street
  closures on Alden Drive between Maple Drive and Foothill Road to host
  Simchat Torah Celebration, which will celebrate both the Jewish holiday
  and remember the lives lost on October 7.
  ii. They are also requesting support for personnel and fee waivers.
  iii. The closures will be from Thursday, October 24th at 5 PM to Friday to
  October 25th at 1 AM.
  iv. Set up for the event would run from 5 PM to 6 PM and cleanup would run
  from 12 AM to 1 AM.
  v. A traffic control officer and meridian barricades would be placed on each
  end of Alden drive for traffic control and event safety.
  vi. Residents and businesses within 500 ft of the event will be notified of the
  street closures two weeks prior to the event.
  vii. The event is not expected to generate additional traffic.
  viii. Total fees and personnel costs from the event will total $6,563.
  b. Three other synagogues aside from Young Israel have agreed to participate in the
  event, with two others waiting on city approval for the road closures before they
  agree to join.
  c. Should all five synagogues participate, event attendance is expected to be
  between 500-600 people.
  d. The Liaisons would like to see the safety considerations raised to the level of other
  city events surrounding 10/7 when the event is presented to the full council.
  e. The liaisons approved the road closure and the fee waivers.

  5) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: August 12, 2024 / 6:55 PM
